headline: Dunning and O'Hare anchor Ward 38, where 7.7 percent of workers commute by bus or train.
summary:
Ward 38 covers Dunning, O'Hare, Portage Park, and part of Belmont Cragin on Chicago's Far Northwest Side. It lands 18th of Chicago's 50 wards on the overall measure, solidly in the upper half of the city. Its strongest numbers touch civic spending and how connected residents feel to their neighbors. Its clearest weak spot is how residents get around town.

The ward posts the best score in Chicago on a measure of pollution near local waterways, and again on schools, the biggest single category in its infrastructure menu spending. It also ranks second for its estimated rate of adult loneliness, one of the lowest readings in Chicago, and second on the ward's trust in local government score. The weak spot is public transit. Only 7.7 percent of workers here commute by bus or train, the lowest share anywhere in Chicago, and the ward also lags on lakefront distance, on a modeled figure, not a headcount, for how often adults see friends, and on how little of its menu budget went to alley repairs.
reading_the_rankings: A few of these numbers carry real qualifiers. First place is less about distance from the pack than it looks, since a full thirty-four wards match this score within two points on the pollution-proximity measure. The trust in local government figure that ranks second has no listed source or description anywhere in the underlying data, so there is no way to say what survey or method produced that number. And the ward's rank of 48th of 50 for lakefront distance only measures how many miles separate Dunning and O'Hare from Lake Michigan, nothing about the neighborhood's condition or upkeep.

news.headline: Boy, 13, Wounded In Portage Park Drive-By Shooting
news.note: A 13-year-old was shot in the leg on the 6000 block of West Montrose Avenue when someone in a passing SUV fired shots, and he was taken to a hospital in good condition.

news.headline: Immigration Agents Crash Into Car, Detain Man In Dunning, Neighbor Says
news.note: A neighbor near Grace Street and Olcott Avenue described federal agents crashing a car during a high-speed chase and detaining a man they identified as the target of an enforcement operation.
